whatItIs.text: An evergreen fruit, botanically a single-seeded berry, with smooth, buttery golden-green flesh. Unlike most fruit it is picked unripe and ripens afterwards.

historyNote.text: Native to the Americas, with archaeological evidence of human use going back thousands of years from Mexico to Peru; in 2024 Mexico alone grew about a quarter of the world's 11.2 million tonnes.

howToChoose.text: Squeeze gently: ripe fruit yields to even, light pressure without feeling mushy, and the stem end should look green underneath, not brown.

storage.text: Let unripe fruit sit on the counter, then move it to the fridge once it yields to pressure.

foodSafetyRef.note: Practice storage guidance only; no rulebook content is claimed. The app's food-safety rules live in data/food-safety/rules.json.

useItUp.text: Overripe avocado blends into dressings, smoothies or chocolate mousse; mash with lime and salt for a two-minute guacamole.

substitutions.note: for toast and spreads; creamier and bean-based rather than creamy-fat
